content:
More than 33,000 Webb County voters have already cast ballots in early voting, the county elections office reported October 28, according to KGNS.

The figure marks a clear step up from the previous update, when early voting stood at nearly 30,000 ballots. It also puts the county on a strong pace with early voting still open: early voting runs through Friday, October 30, ahead of Election Day on Tuesday, November 3.

The timing matters. The November 3 ballot includes the Laredo mayor's race, City Council seats in Districts 1, 2, 3 and 6, and Municipal Court Judge Place 1, along with county, state and federal contests. Voters who have not yet cast a ballot still have the rest of the early-voting window to do so at any early-voting location in the county where they are registered.

Turnout figures count ballots cast, not choices made. They show how many people have voted, not how any race is trending — a distinction that matters in a week when statewide and local campaigns are both pushing supporters to the polls before the early-voting deadline.

What to watch next: the final early-voting total when polls close October 30, and how that total compares with the last comparable election once Election Day votes are added.

Sources:

  • KGNS, “Webb County elections office reports more than 33,000 early voters so far,” October 28, 2026

title: Webb County early voting passes 33,000 as final early-voting days arrive
